about: KoolKisaan Flowers – final design (ice panels) on the seasonal loading plan. Headline = best practice.

date_range.label: 1 Jan 2026 – 6 Nov 2026 (310 days, real Visakhapatnam weather, digital twin)

note: Digital twin (S) on real 2026 Visakhapatnam weather. Nothing here is measured. E = assumption (config/design.json -> assumptions_E, data/crops.json, data/season_calendar.json).

design.name: KoolKisaan Flowers
design.tagline: Cold from the sun, ice for the night, truth in the ledger.

extra_racks.aisle_note: two side racks: aisle only about 0.49 m (tight, E)

assumptions_E.glycol.cp_kJ_kgK: E – 30-35 % propylene glycol near 0 C: about 3.7 kJ/kg.K (design brief; check the glycol supplier's data sheet).
assumptions_E.glycol.freeze_C: E – 30-35 % propylene glycol freezes at about -13 C (design brief; check the data sheet).
assumptions_E.glycol.hx_approach_K: E – brazed-plate heat exchanger approach 3 K: R290 evaporating temperature = glycol supply - 3 K (design brief).
assumptions_E.glycol.supply_room_C: E – glycol supply about 0 C when only the air cooler is fed (design brief).
assumptions_E.glycol.supply_ice_C: E – glycol supply about -5 C when the ice is being made (R290 then evaporates at -8 C). 30-35 % glycol freezes at about -13 C, so this is safe.
assumptions_E.glycol.design_dT_K: E – glycol warms 3 K at full 1.5 kW load; this sets the fixed pump flow (our choice, typical 3-5 K).
assumptions_E.glycol.pump_W: E – 18 W electronically commutated DC pump (the first design had a plain 40 W pump), runs only with the chiller; same glycol flow assumed. All of it is counted as heat into the glycol (conservative).
assumptions_E.glycol.pipe_UA_W_K: E – chiller within 1.5 m of the wall (3 m of pipe in total), 32 mm nitrile insulation, insulated tank and plate exchanger: 1.0 W/K to the outside air (first design: 6 m of pipe, 19 mm insulation, 3 W/K). Chosen by results/live/pipe_pump.json.
assumptions_E.glycol.air_cooler_G_kW_K: E – glycol air cooler with EC fan: 900 m3/h of air (0.32 kW/K), effectiveness about 0.78 -> 0.25 kW per K between room air and mean glycol temperature (our estimate; check the chosen unit).
assumptions_E.glycol.air_cooler_air_side_frac: E – 75 % of the air cooler's heat resistance is on the air side, so the wet fin surface is warmer than the glycol: T_surface = T_room - 0.75 x (T_room - T_glycol_mean). This decides how much water the coil takes out of the air (our estimate, typical finned coil).
assumptions_E.glycol.ice_coil_R_m2K_W: E – contact resistance of the coils in the ice panels, same value as the old twin (0.01 m2K/W).
assumptions_E.glycol.loop_volume_L: E – about 15 L of glycol in pipes, coils and tank (our estimate). Used only in the reality check (re-cooling the loop at every start).
assumptions_E.product.pulldown_hours: E – flowers in ventilated crates lose 7/8 of their extra warmth in 4 h (same rule as the old twin; flowers are light, so this is likely conservative).
assumptions_E.door: E – 6 door openings a day (05:00, 05:10, 09:00, 13:00, 13:10, 17:00), 20 s each, strip curtain 85 % effective (design brief + old twin).
assumptions_E.live_run.load_hour: E – unsold surplus is loaded at 13:00 at that hour's outside air temperature and taken out at 05:00 (design brief).
assumptions_E.live_run.sun_factor: E – sunlight x 0.88 (old twin: Open-Meteo corrected to the NASA POWER level).
assumptions_E.controller.protect_above_C: E – grid help when the room stays above 6.0 C (top of the normal band) for 15 min, off again below 5.0 C (our rule). results/live/night_limit.json shows what 5.5 and 6.5 C would give.
assumptions_E.humidity.liner_transpiration_factor: E – perforated polyethylene crate liners cut the water loss of the flowers to about 25 % of the unlined value (literature for perforated film liners: 50-90 % less weight loss).
assumptions_E.humidity.tray: E – open water tray 0.5 m2 on the floor, natural convection 4 W/m2K (our estimate).
assumptions_E.humidity.fogger: E – ultrasonic fogger 0.30 L/h, 30 W, switched on below 90 % RH and off at 95 % (design brief + typical small unit). Needs clean (RO) water.
assumptions_E.humidity.flower_air_speed: E – air speed around the flowers 0.5 m/s with the cooler fan on, 0.1 m/s with it off (our estimate).
assumptions_E.simulation.structure_heat_capacity_kJ_K: E – 60 kJ/K for the inner skin of the room (old twin).
assumptions_E.simulation.inverter_min_capacity_frac: E – inverter chiller runs between 30 % and 100 % (old twin).
assumptions_E.pcm.ice: E – water with a nucleating agent freezes and melts at about 0 C, latent heat 334 kJ/kg (textbook value). Conductivity of liquid water 0.6 W/m.K is used for the whole slab (careful: ice is 2.2). Water grows 9 % when it freezes: the panels need room for that.
assumptions_E.pcm.fixed_cost_INR: E – water costs about nothing; Rs 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 for nucleating agent, biocide and leak-tight containers.
assumptions_E.pcm.charge_stop_C: E – charging stops when the ice is 1 K below freezing.
assumptions_E.reality.racks: E – rack masses, heat capacities and prices (FRP, HDPE, steel).
assumptions_E.reality.best.door: E – best practice: 4 door openings a day (05:00, 05:10, 06:00, 06:10), 20 s, good curtain (85 %) and a door closer.
assumptions_E.reality.best.load_hour: E – best practice: flowers are loaded at 06:00 (cool morning, a full day of sun ahead), never 11:00-15:00.
assumptions_E.reality.best.night_fan: E – 12 W EC circulation fan runs when the chiller is off and the room is more than 0.5 K above the set-point; it doubles the heat flow from the fins (mixed convection, our estimate); its power comes from the grid at night and is counted.
assumptions_E.reality.poor.roof_solar: E – poor practice: no shade, dark roof (absorptance 0.7, outside film 20 W/m2K, 4.84 m2).
assumptions_E.reality.poor.floor: E – poor practice: floor not insulated: 3.1 W/K extra to ground at 28 C (concrete on soil about 1.0 W/m2K instead of 0.22, 4 m2).
assumptions_E.controller.low_stop_C: Controller lower limit: the air cooler valve (V-ROOM) closes when the room reaches 3.0 C and opens again at 4.5 C, so the chiller never pulls the room below 3 C.
assumptions_E.flowers.respiration_above_20C: E – respiration heat is held at the 20 C table value above 20 C (no data there) and fades in step with the freshness that is left.
